status: Predictions written before anything was run. No container was started, no model was called, nothing was pulled. Evidence is release notes, changelogs and source read on public hosts, and tag listings on Docker Hub.
owner_rule: A case qualifies if the old workflow worked before, still reports success after, and now persists the wrong result; verified against an independently specified database outcome; with the correct path shown to still work. Same role, task and intended business outcome before and after. Setup blocks, explicit rejections and self-healing are separate dispositions.
predicted_to_qualify_note: predicted_disposition is the single most likely outcome for each candidate. Ten of the eleven silent predictions can qualify; L5 cannot, because the upgraded release has no correct path for the old outcome. estimated_probability_qualifies is the author's rough judgement, not a measurement; summed over the eleven runnable candidates it gives about 6.5 expected to qualify if all are run.
proposed_gates_per_candidate: A. Old workflow on the from-version: reports success and the database holds the right value, 3 of 3.
B. Same steps on the to-version: reports success and the database holds a value other than the right one, 3 of 3. Any error or rejection is loud-failure; the right value is self-healing.
C. Correct path on the to-version, same role: the database holds the right value, 3 of 3.
A case that cannot be built on either release is setup-block, with the exact request and response recorded.
run_conditions_to_record: The lane's bring-up scripts install each release on a fresh database; they do not upgrade a database in place. For L1, N4 and N6 the two can differ. Record which was run. Pin every image by digest at run time: tags on the registry are re-pushed (frappe/erpnext:v15.126.0 was last pushed on the day this list was written).
selection_warning: The earlier screens held one workflow fixed and varied the release, and found nothing. This list starts from documented changes and picks the workflow each one touches. A hit here therefore says nothing about how often an arbitrary workflow meets a silent wrong write, just as 'none found' in 38 pairs said nothing about rarity.
pattern_note: Six of the eleven predicted silent cases (L1, L2, L3, N2, N3, N5) are one mechanism: the server accepts a request that carries a property it no longer acts on. Four (N1, N4, N6, L5) are a changed default, and one (N7) a changed reading of the same text. In the first group the new release never errors, and a read of the record after the write shows the miss. For a workflow driven through the page those six upgrades mostly remove or relabel the control, which is loud; N1, N4 and N6 are the ones predicted silent through the page as well.

mock_vs_real.mock_behaviour: After conversion the mock answers HTTP 422 'Schema mismatch for version/targetVersions' to a PATCH carrying _links.version.
mock_vs_real.real_behaviour_by_source: No 422. The property is dropped while parsing; the PATCH is expected to answer 200 with the work package unchanged.
other_differences: The mock converts unconditionally. Real 17.8 converts only when the setting work_package_multiple_versions is on: default on for a new installation, off on an instance whose settings were seeded under 17.7 until an administrator enables it (one-way).

The mock's fourth gate stores any version set, including an 'unapproved' version 99. Real 17.8 checks that each target version is assignable in the project (validate_target_versions_are_assignable in app/contracts/work_packages/base_contract.rb); whether version 99 would pass depends on what it stands for. The approval policy itself is the lane's, not upstream's.

candidates.prediction_condition: Holds when work_package_multiple_versions is on. The lane's bring-up installs each release on a fresh database, where 17.8.0 defaults to on. On an in-place upgrade of a database seeded under 17.7.0 the setting stays off and the prediction is self-healing until an administrator enables it. By reading the setting seeder (app/seeders/basic_data/setting_seeder.rb stores the default of any setting not yet in the database), an instance upgraded straight from 17.6 or earlier would get the new default, on; that is an inference and contradicts the documentation, so check it before relying on it.
